- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., -0.11 or lower) in recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward — adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid excessive sell-off bias.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+1.5% from prior day), model often overshoots and fails to mean-revert — reduce forecast peak by 5–10% and add a slight downward slope to avoid overcorrection.  
- If sentiment is positive and price is trending upward, model often underestimates the continuation — increase forecast by 2–5% for the next 3–5 days to capture momentum.  
- Model consistently underestimates true price in early days of a 30-day horizon — especially when sentiment is neutral or slightly positive — add 0.5–1.5% to initial forecast to account for lag.  
- When sentiment history shows repeated small negative swings, model tends to ignore them — apply a mild upward bias (e.g., +0.2–0.5) to counteract mean-reversion bias.
